EDIT: BOOM! Got it working. To scared to mess with anything else for now. Server block was pointing to a child directory, I was in the parent directory, thus a permission denied.

I'm not familiar with your distribution, but based on your configs, it looks you aren't using a "standard" location for the web server document root, so I'm guessing you made it yourself? Does Antergos come with SELinux installed and configured? Because that will bite you in the ass unless you apply the proper context to those directories... or just disable SELinux or its analog in your distro.

As far as I know Antergos does not come with SELinux. I ran some commands to check but I forget what they were, I tried a bunch of different things. It comes down to a permissions issue I believe, I just couldn't figure it out.

Yeah, it's definitely that, but your permissions look good. What user is running nginx? The same one that owns all those files/directories? Can you su over to that user (give it a shell temporarily if you have to) and see if you can navigate that directory tree and cat those files? If that all works, then you have to start looking at things like mount permissions and things like that: is /home on its own mount, and if so, do you have any restrictions on it in /etc/fstab?
